Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: sam123ben
Message:
fix(payments): resolve the Cashfree host from the credentials, not the slot

Cashfree separates sandbox from production by hostname, and the host was bound to
the platform's live/test partition. That made it the odd gateway out: Razorpay
decides its environment from the key prefix, so its live slot runs test keys
perfectly happily, while Cashfree's live slot holding sandbox keys produced a
valid client that 401'd against api.cashfree.com. Every live checkout therefore
fell back to Razorpay, and Cashfree could not be exercised at all until real live
credentials existed.

The host now follows the credentials. Cashfree marks both halves — sandbox App
IDs are prefixed TEST and sandbox secrets carry _test_ — and either signal is
enough, so a rotation that changes one format cannot silently flip an
environment.

The two directions are deliberately NOT symmetric:

  - LIVE slot + sandbox credentials -> sandbox. Harmless, and the normal state
    while a merchant account is in review.
  - TEST slot -> sandbox ALWAYS, whatever the credentials say. Honouring a
    production credential there would let a sandbox order move real money, and
    for the payouts rail reach a real bank account. That is the one outcome
    worth hard-coding against.

So the failure direction is always "test money does not move", never "real money
moves unexpectedly".

Both admin warnings are corrected with it. They claimed live payments would fail
with 401, which is now false — the keys work, against the sandbox. The useful
warning is not that payments fail but that they succeed while capturing nothing
real, which is a far easier thing to miss.

Verified against the live sandbox: the live-slot credentials from Secret Manager
now authenticate (404 on a nonexistent order, which is the authenticated
response).

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Samyak Rout
Message:
fix(payments): resolve the Cashfree host from the credentials, not the slot (#853)

* test(web): cover the cart page rendering with items in it

The cart page went to a blank error-boundary screen in production and nothing
caught it, because no test had ever mounted this page with a populated cart —
typecheck passes happily on JSX that throws at render.

(The production failure turned out to be a stale chunk after a deploy, not the
page itself. The gap it exposed is real either way: the page had no render
coverage at all, so a genuine break would have looked identical and been
diagnosed just as slowly.)

Adds a localStorage backing to the shared vitest setup rather than to the test.
zustand's persist middleware binds its storage when the store module is first
imported, which happens before any test body runs, so a per-test stub is too
late — and the resulting failure points at zustand internals rather than at the
component under test, which is a bad first impression for anyone writing the
next store-backed test.

* feat(web): let customers change their order from checkout

Checkout was a one-way door. The Order Summary listed what you were about to pay
for but offered no way to change it, and the header cart link is hidden on this
route — so a customer who changed their mind at the last step had nowhere to go
but the browser's back button.

Each line now carries a remove control, and the block links back to the cart.

Removing the last line is handled by the guard that was already there: an empty
cart redirects to /cart, so the customer lands on the cart's empty state rather
than a checkout for nothing.

This is the affordance the previous commit added to the cart page, at the place
customers actually hesitate. Reviewing the order and deciding against part of it
happens at checkout, not on the way there.

Author: sam123ben
Message:
chore(mobile-admin): add Firebase config for com.tesserix.homechef.admin

The admin app uses native @react-native-firebase/auth (GIP sign-in via the shared
auth module), so the iOS/Android builds need the Firebase config for its bundle id.
Registered iOS + Android apps for com.tesserix.homechef.admin in the shared
Firebase project (tesseracthub-480811) and committed the config, matching how
customer/vendor already commit theirs. Dropped the per-app .gitignore rules that
were excluding them (customer/vendor don't ignore these). Unblocks the EAS build.

Description: Uncovered a GCP API key, which could lead to unauthorized access to Google Cloud services and data breaches.
Author: sam123ben
Message:
feat(mobile-admin): admin/owner console app + EAS build job

New apps/mobile-admin Expo app (iOS + Android) — a native admin/owner console
mirroring the web admin portal, built on the mobile-vendor template
(@homechef/mobile-shared, @tesserix/native, expo-router) and integrated to the
existing Go API via the auth-bff (/auth/auto-login + /api/v1/admin/*).

Screens: Dashboard, Chefs (verify/reject/suspend), Orders, Approvals
(approve/reject/request-info + home-chef non-home-kitchen & FSSAI-commercial
review aids), Users (suspend/activate), FSSAI lockouts (override/clear),
Reviews (hide/unhide), Wallets (credit/debit adjust), Meal Plans, Delivery,
Staff (invite/de-/re-activate), Analytics, Settings. 12 React Query hooks over
/admin/*; ink-centric design per .impeccable.md. tsc --noEmit clean.

Auth: Firebase/GIP tenant HomeChef-Internal-gyofe (internal pool -> admin role).
Adds that tenant to the auth-bff mobileTenantAllowlist (homechef-products.yaml)
so admin mobile logins are accepted; requires an auth-bff redeploy.

Also adds 'admin' to the homechef-mobile-build EAS workflow (app choice +
all-matrix).
